message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 and a fully built pink monopoly. The opponent on North Carolina Avenue has a dangerous dark blue monopoly and only $29 cash. Player 3 is bankrupt.

Player 4 has $763 and a light blue monopoly. The auction is at $117 with p2 and p4 as bidders. I will cap my bid near $150 to mortgage the green and deny player 4 a second green.

Bidding $118 nets $32 profit after mortgaging the property for $150. This makes the auction cash-positive while blocking player 4.

Neither player can complete a green monopoly alone. Player 1 holds Pacific, and I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue. Denying player 4 North Carolina Avenue prevents them from pairing it with Pacific to trade for a monopoly.

I am on Pennsylvania Avenue. The next spaces are Short Line, Chance, Park Place, Luxury Tax, and Boardwalk. Landing on Park Place would cost $1100 against my $726 cash. I could sell houses from my pink monopoly to cover the shortfall.

Selling all twelve pink houses would return $600, but that still leaves a gap against the $1700 Boardwalk rent. I will raise my bid to about $149 or $150. This gives me the cash needed to survive the dark blue hits while blocking player 4.

I will raise to the minimum $118. Player 4 has matched every bid so far and likely has enough cash to keep bidding past my $150 cap. I will continue with small raises to extract as much money as possible from them. A jump bid would risk overpaying if they drop out soon.
